english:
My name is Akash Alexander. This is my mother Philomina. This is my wife Shobiya. We have come from Coimbatore.
First of all, I thank God and the Mother who stood this family as a testimony. It was my mother who first took the Covenant here at this Kreupasanam.
She took the Covenant and prayed saying that prayers should be offered for her children. But we had no interest in it.
We had no faith at all. We were just Christians who went to church for name’s sake. That was all we had.
But God showed us that whenever we walk forgetting God, God will question us in return. Last year, in this same month—January month— my mother started bleeding.
But she did not tell us. She was bleeding. January passed, February passed, March passed.
For three months, my mother had bleeding, but she did not tell us. On April 1st, my mother collapsed, and only then she told us— that this is what she has.
At that very moment, we began to tremble. Immediately, on April 2nd, I took her to the hospital.
When we told the doctor, he said my mother had only six percent blood. The blood was not staying in her body. “What were you doing all these months?” he asked and scolded us severely.
Along with that, he said one more thing—that there is a possibility my mother has cancer.
Even hearing such a word shook us. Ten days later, when the biopsy report came, they said it is cancer, third stage.
We had no idea at all what to do. Even then, I did not call upon the Lord.
I did not call upon the Lord asking what to do. I thought, “It’s a hospital, right? Let’s see, let’s see.” My mother remained in bed for one month.
Urine tube and motion—everything was on the bed itself.
She could not get up from the bed. She was bedridden. After one month, the doctor came and said— “Your mother will not return.” He asked to pray.
That is when, inside my mind, a thought came—“Oh, there is something called prayer.” Saying,
“Why did we not remember this?”—from that moment, in the month of May, I came and sat alone at the far corner. I did not even go inside. I was alone there.
I sat there looking at the face of the Mother. I did not pray. Tears began to flow from my eyes.
I do not know how. I did not even pray properly, but tears started flowing. Then I spoke to the Mother as if I was just talking casually.
I said, “I should bring my mother here. Only then will I take the Covenant here.” That is what I said. I did not pray—I just spoke.
The very next week, my mother got down from the bed. The urine tube was removed. A change began to come in my mother.
Even then, I did not fully understand it. The following week, the doctor came—the same doctor who had said, “She will not stay with us longer” That doctor was astonished,
The body that had only 6% blood now had 9%. He asked how this was possible.
Then, the very next month, on June 24th, I took the Covenant here. I brought my mother here and took the Covenant.
That was the correction the Mother gave me. It was a correction for saying that I forgot the Lord and the Mother.
I directly brought my mother here, took the Covenant, stood before the Father, prayed, received prayer with the laying on of hands, and then took her back.
The very next month, she was discharged from the hospital and came home. I did not give my mother even a single tablet of medicine.
Using only blessed salt, honey, and holy oil, I took care of my mother. I stayed with her and looked after her.
After three months, when it was time to come for renewing, I came here again and sat here and prayed. I sat inside and prayed.
What I prayed for was this—that when I come next time, there should be nothing in my mother’s report.
Just like that, the doctor said there was nothing in the PET scan.
Truly, the Mother touched my mother well, and she touched our family well. We who had no faith are now living in faith, and family prayer is happening at home without interruption.
We participate in every adoration. We fast and pray. Now my mother has 11 percent blood in her body.
Even now, my mother does not take any tablets or medicines. We have only our prayers. I have brought my mother here so that she may say a few words of prayer.
I do not know how to say it. My prayer is a prayer that began 36 years ago.
My son did not remain with me in prayer, but I have one desire—that they should pray.
For that purpose, many things began from the beginning, and step by step, step by step, the Lord kept drawing me forward.
At that time also, when I go with the rosary and when I return, when I go to work, when I sit—everywhere there is the rosary. In that prayer, the Mother is also there.
As things went on like that, a thought came to me—that they are not participating in prayer because they do not know how to pray.
While I was like that, I tried telling them and explaining, but I believe God showed them a sign meant for them.
Moreover, after one month, when my mother was in the hospital and almost a month had passed— at a time when I had no one,
a doctor and a nurse came to me. They asked me everything, but I could not say anything. The nurse explained everything.
Immediately, the doctor told the nurse, “Shift her from this ward and take her there. I will look after her,” and he left. He said, “I will look after her,” and went.
After that, the ward was changed, everything was done, scans were taken, and all procedures were completed.
Only later did I realize that I did not know anything about the things the doctor had told my son earlier. I did not even know that it was the Mother who had come.
Still, I did not say anything. Later I understood. That one word—“I will look after her”—remained deeply in my heart.
Even now, at three in the morning, after so many years, it is still the same. I get up praying and pray for hours.
I was in a prayer that the prayer of children should always be present there.
After that, when we came home and then returned three months later to renew the Covenant, after that they themselves began to pray.
Whether it was in English, Malayalam, or what they call Manglish, they bought a book and began to pray on their own.
When it is time for prayer, they call me, “mother come, let us begin the prayer,” and they come. What I have to say now is this: I am someone who cannot stand straight, who remains bent like this.
I cannot stand upright. Only if three people support me can I stand or walk.
When I was like that, my son and daughter together resigned from their jobs, stayed with me, took care of me, and even now both of them continue to strive and work for me.
That Mother is with us. We can never finish thanking the Lord and the Holy Mother, even with crores and crores of thanks.
And when we speak about the mission activities—right from the beginning, it started from the time my son was born.
When his birthday came, there would be money to buy him clothes, cake, and other things. I never did that.
I kept that money aside and took it to orphanages and gave it there, arranging food for them.
Every year, I would do this. I would sit with them, eat one meal together with them, and then return. That itself is my son’s birthday function—a blessing.
In the same way, even now, if it is for ten people, we will take food for ten people and give it.
And when we go to church, we buy rice and give it there so that food can be prepared.
In the same manner, in all matters of our life, we have been doing things like this—mission activities, distributing newsletters, and giving help in hospitals and everywhere.
To God the Father who guided us, protected us, carried us, and led us all along the way— to our Lord Jesus Christ, and to our Mother, and to the Mother who interceded for us— we offer crores and crores and crores of thanks, and with that gratitude, I conclude my words.
He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has saved you. Go in peace. Be freed from your illness.” This is from the Gospel of Mark, chapter 5, verse 34.
The Lord said this to a woman who had been suffering from bleeding for twelve years - "Your faith has made you well".
Her body was weak. All her hopes had faded away.
Yet, a small faith—that if she could just touch the garment of Jesus, she would be healed—was present in her.
Jesus did not say, “By my power, filled with strength, I have healed you.” He did not say, “It is by my power that I healed you.” Instead, the Lord said, “Your faith has saved you.”
The Blessed Mother is a great witness of faith. “Do whatever He tells you”—this is what the Holy Mother taught us.
To each and every person who comes to this sanctuary, who comes into this presence— to all the children who take the Covenant here— the Blessed Mother is saying the same thing: “Do whatever He tells you.”
It is the Blessed Mother who leads us with faith towards Jesus.
In moments when we do not know how long-term illnesses and health problems will move forward— the Lord calls us,
“My daughter, my son.” When we pray with faith, we return joyfully from this sanctuary. Those who come here with tears leave this sanctuary in peace.
Such a great testimony is what the son Akash Alexander has shared with us— about a bleeding that continued for three months, in a very dangerous situation.
The mother did not tell anyone. This mother, who was in the Covenant, later suddenly collapsed, and only then did the children come to know. They rushed her to the hospital.
Later, this son did not have much faith. He would pray, but it was the life and habits of an ordinary Christian— perhaps only a name.
Later, even in that condition, the mother did not feel like praying.
But after all the treatments, the doctor said one thing: the chances of saving the mother are very less. The words “Pray for her” attracted this son deeply and caused great pain.
That single word—“Pray”—the doctor’s final words—were what brought this son, with tears, into the presence of this Mother.
Even when this son came here the first time, he did not feel like praying. He said, “I did not pray; I only spoke to the Mother.”
This speaking itself is prayer—what we say to the Mother from our mind, from our heart, from the depth of our suffering—that is prayer.
The son says he only spoke, but that speaking became prayer. It was this prayer that the Mother took to Jesus.
“I will bring my mother here. Heal my mother and bring her to this sanctuary”—this is what this son cried and spoke in prayer to the Blessed Mother,
sitting and weeping in this holy presence where the Blessed Mother appeared. Later, after seeing the priest, this son returned, within one week the mother received a good healing.
The hemoglobin that was at six suddenly rose to nine, and now it has become eleven.
All this happened so quickly. The Mother is waiting just for one word from us.
When this son prayed with a complete mind and with his whole heart, the Mother immediately took over everything concerning this son. What followed was a sudden healing.
The Lord who said, “Your faith has saved you,” affirmed it on the foundation of this daughter. This daughter had prayed in the Covenant. She has a strong foundation— a foundation of much prayer,
a life of sacrifice, and a Covenant life. It was on that foundation that Jesus said to this daughter, “Your faith has saved you.” Along with that,
not only her faith, but also the faith of the children prepared the situation today— to bring them into this presence and to stand them here as witnesses.
No child who comes close to the Blessed Mother has ever gone away in sorrow. The Mother who is with us is one who takes those who come in tears by the hand and leads them forward.
Children who are in the covenant only need to pray with a good heart. What was also said later is that only Covenant items were used.
All medicines were stopped. Using only the Covenant items—this son came with a good faithfulness.
Though it took time, when the son came with faith, he came with a strong and firm faith. After taking the Covenant, only the Covenant items were used for the mother.
Only after that did the hemoglobin become normal—11. And it happened very quickly. Immediately after taking the Covenant, when this son came for the first renewal and then the second renewal,
he said, “My mother’s report should come as negative.” Everything that followed happened after taking the Covenant. This son’s faith reached a milestone—he spoke firmly to the Mother,
saying, “I want this, I want that,” just like a son speaking to his own mother. When he went after the renewal, he said clearly, “My mother’s next report should be negative.”
In the same way, the Blessed Mother spoke to Jesus and made it happen. This is how every matter in our life is.
Even when time seems delayed, even when we feel we do not have time, even when everything seems to have ended or is about to end, Jesus and the Mother—who never abandon us—are with us.
Jesus calls us “son” and “daughter.” Even in our broken moments and situations, He calls us “son” and “daughter.” Let us give thanks for that love.
Let us remain united in that love. Through the Blessed Mother, let us remain united in faith, and move forward peacefully, living the Covenant life with sincerity.
Let us pray that Jesus and the Mother may help us in this. For the great blessing received by the family of Akash Alexander,
let us clap our hands and glorify God. Jesus, thank You. Jesus, praise You.
